content:
maria: Quick heads-up — after we enabled the continuous microbatch saga mode on a canary pool (11:20) we saw short-request tail latency spike. p50 steady (~45ms) but p95 jumped 95 -> ~210ms. Dash: https://dash/reports/ci/1769998001 :thinking:

sam: Is it tenant-localized or cross-tenant? Any error counts?

maria: Cross-tenant on hosted. No errors, just longer waits. No OOMs, GPUs at normal occupancy.

alex: Logs show saga commit flows holding kvcache references while waiting for manager ack. Eviction churn right after commit_start in many traces. Snippet:

```
[2026-03-19T11:22:05Z] microbatch_saga: commit_start tenant=acct-42 req=0x7fae
[2026-03-19T11:22:05Z] kvcache: evict key=model-bert:slot-11
[2026-03-19T11:22:05Z] microbatch_saga: waiting on postCommitFuture req=0x7fae
[2026-03-19T11:22:05Z] kvcache: miss tenant=acct-42 key=model-bert:slot-11
```

alex: Host threads show idle gaps waiting on commit ack; GPU work mostly fine.

patrick: Canary config used window_ms=8, max_coalesce=64? If saga increases commit latency we might desync coalesce boundaries and split otherwise-coalesced requests.

maria: Lowered window_ms to 4ms on a small subset — p50 improved slightly but p95 remained high. Traces show short requests getting split across microbatches then blocked on saga wait.

sam: Been able to rollback?

maria: We toggled saga off on one canary and tail returned to baseline. So rollback works as a mitigation.

alex: Short-term fixes we can iterate: 1) make commit path async (early-ack) for tiny requests; 2) reduce strong refs during commit so kvcache can evict; 3) gate saga for tenants flagged as latency-sensitive. Tradeoffs: async commit risks ordering/consistency; weak refs might complicate correctness assumptions.

sam: If we do async early-ack, must ensure no observable ordering violations. Maybe restrict to stateless handlers or requests that don't mutate shared metadata.

alex: Agreed. Prototype flag microbatch_saga.commit_async=true limited to seq_len <= 8 and add sampled linearizability checks.

maria: Can share config we ran on canary B:

```
microbatch_saga:
  enabled: true
  window_ms: 8
  max_coalesce: 64
  commit_async: false
```

maria: Enabling commit_async in local perf harness reduced p95, but a canary ordering unit test failed when we tried it end-to-end.

patrick: Also audit the kvcache pin semantics. If saga holds a hard reference until ack, that prevents LRU eviction and then the next churn becomes expensive. Options: convert to weak refs, move refs to a small staging cache, or limit saga lifetime.

infra-bot: Noted elevated eviction_rate on g-102 at 11:21:40 and node io_wait climb. Logs: https://logs/redwood/g-102/1769998001

deploy-bot: Canary roll 1769998001 -> microbatch-saga started; rolled back on canary-2 after perf regress.

sam: Proposed next steps (short):
- Run microbench matrix: window_ms in {2,4,8} x commit_async {on,off}. Measure p50/p95, kvcache hitrate, eviction_rate, saga_hold_time.
- Add telemetry counter histogram `saga_hold_time_ms` (commit_start -> commit_release) per-tenant sampled.
- Implement commit_async prototype gated by seq_len <= 8 + opt-in tenant flag.
- Add sampled ordering validator comparing logical commit order vs observed, fail experiment if mismatch rate > 1e-4.

maria: I'll open a concise experiment RFC and assign owners. Recommend we disable saga in hosted until commit_async safety is proven; rollback is trivial.

alex: I'll own commit_async prototype and the ordering validator.

patrick: I'll audit kvcache ref lifecycle and try a weak-ref/staging approach.

maria: Scheduling 30m sync tomorrow to review RFC and experiment plan. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
